fact: La Nation reports that HOOM, an AI-based education application conceived and developed by Djiboutians, is already used by more than 4,500 terminale pupils, about 57% of the year group, and includes the KékéBot teaching assistant.

Minister Mariam Hamadou Ali says the LinkWise integrated project, financed in full (US$1.35bn) by Shanghai LinkWise and Shanghai Nenghui Technology on 1,000 hectares granted by the government, will build a 100 MW intelligent computing centre (AIDC) using NVIDIA H and B series chips, with first-phase construction and commissioning expected within three years of an MOU valid for one year.

fact: Djibouti's labour minister met LinkWise on the planned AI compute infrastructure, projected at about 2,000 construction jobs and 500 to 700 skilled operating posts, still to be confirmed by studies (ADI).
The Djibouti Ports and Free Zones Authority says DPCR Vision AI, an AI road-defect detector, was developed by Djibouti Ports Corridor Road and launched in 2024.
DPCR says it developed CorridorVision AI, training a YOLOv8 detection model on road images its annotators labelled, and deployed it on the RapidCanvas platform.

The University of Djibouti's AI research laboratory LaRIA held a workshop on 9 July 2026 exhibiting its AI projects, including cancer-cell detection and demonstrations of early-warning systems for disasters and epidemics.

Africa Insight reports that on 6 April 2026 the University of Djibouti (CRMN and CEALT) and Jamhuuriya University launched the Somali-Language AI & Innovation Lab (SAIL) and a Somali fake-news detection research project using NLP and deep learning, with machine translation and voice assistants as long-term aims.
